'''''Heptapleurum arboricola''''' (syn. ''[[Schefflera]] arboricola'', {{Lang-zh|c=鹅掌藤|p=ézhǎng téng|l=goose-sole vine}}) is a [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Araliaceae]], native to [[Hainan]] Province, China and [[Taiwan]].<ref name="POWO_90845-1" >{{cite POWO |id=90845-1 |title=''Heptapleurum arboricola'' Hayata |access-date=8 January 2023 }}</ref><ref name=FoT>{{cite book |title=Flora of Taiwan |edition=2nd |volume=3 |chapter=Araliaceae |last1=Ohashi |first1=Hiroyoshi |editor-last=Huang |editor-first=Tseng-chieng |year=1993 |publisher=Editorial Committee of the Flora of Taiwan, Second Edition |location=Taipei, Taiwan |isbn=957-9019-41-X |page=1002 |url=http://tai2.ntu.edu.tw/ebook/ebookcontent.php?book=Fl.%20Taiwan%202nd%20edit.&volume=3 |chapter-url=http://tai2.ntu.edu.tw/ebook/ebookpage.php?volume=3&book=Fl.%20Taiwan%202nd%20edit.&page=1002 |access-date=14 March 2013}}</ref><ref name=FoC>{{cite web |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200015275 |title=''Schefflera arboricola'' |author=Qibai Xiang & Porter P. Lowry |work=Flora of China |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden, St. Louis, MO & Harvard University Herbaria, Cambridge, MA |access-date=14 March 2013}}</ref> Its common name is '''dwarf umbrella tree''', as it resembles a smaller version of the umbrella tree, ''[[Heptapleurum actinophyllum]]''.<ref name = GRIN>{{GRIN}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Schefflera sp., Gran Canaria.jpg|thumb|Fruits]]
It is an [[evergreen]] shrub growing to 8–9 m tall, free-standing, or clinging to the trunks of other trees as an [[epiphyte]]. The leaves are [[palmate]]ly compound, with 7–9 leaflets, the leaflets 9–20 cm long and 4–10 cm broad (though often smaller in cultivation) with a wedge-shaped base, entire margin, and an obtuse or acute apex, sometimes emarginate.<ref name=FoT/><ref name=FoC/> The leaves are leathery in texture, shiny green, [[Glabrousness (botany)|glabrous]] on the upper surface and somewhat lighter and matte on the underside. Young plants have smaller leaves and fewer leaflets. Each leaflet has a central rib that divides it into two halves, with between four and six ribs clearly visible up to the third order. The [[stipule]]s merge with the [[petiole (botany)|petiole]], the length of which is 12-15 cm.<ref name="Clemson">{{cite web |last1=Russ |first1=Karen |last2=Pertuit |first2=Al |title=Schefflera |url=https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/schefflera-2/ |website=Clemson Cooperative Extension Home & Garden Information Center |access-date=5 May 2020}}</ref>

===Flowers===
Appearing from midsummer to early autumn, the flowers are produced in a 20 cm [[panicle]] of small [[umbel]]s, each umbel 7–10 mm in diameter with 5–10 flowers.<ref name=FoT/> The flowers are [[hermaphroditic]], having a colour ranging from yellow to green and a double [[perianth]] radial symmetry. They are composed of an entire annular [[Calyx (botany)|calyx]], five almost fully developed [[sepal]]s, a [[corolla (botany)|corolla]] with five petals 2.5 mm long, with five [[stamen]]s and five or six [[carpel]]s that enclose the [[Ovary (botany)|ovary]]. The style is not recognizable and the [[stigma (botany)|stigma]] is established.<ref name=FoC/>

===Fruits===
The fruits have an almost spherical oval [[drupe]], with a diameter of about 5 mm. The [[endocarp]] contains five seeds. The fruits ripen from late summer to early winter. They begin as orange glandular points. At maturity, they become red-violet. The fruits are inedible to humans,<ref name="knight2007">{{cite book |last1=Knight |first1=Anthony |title=A guide to poisonous house and garden plants |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Fi_lAgAAQBAJ&q=schefflera |access-date=14 December 2024 |pages=245–246 |date=2007 |publisher=CRC Press |isbn=978-1-59161-028-1 }}</ref> but may be consumed (and spread elsewhere) by various birds or other animals.<ref name="purificacao2015">{{cite journal |author1=Purificação, K. N. |author2=Pascotto, M.C. |author3=Mohr, A. |author4=Lenza, E. |title=Frugivory by birds on Schefflera morototoni (Araliaceae) in a Cerrado-Amazon forest transition area, eastern Mato Grosso, Brazil |journal=Acta Amazonica |date=2015 |volume=45 |issue=1 |pages=57–64 |doi=10.1590/1809-4392201402402 |bibcode=2015AcAma..45...57P |quote=...23 bird species were recorded consuming...fruits. Out of these, 20 bird species were considered potential seed dispersers, as they swallow the fruits whole.|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Distribution==
This species is indigenous to Taiwan and has been introduced to the Ryukyu Islands, Hawaii, Florida, Bermuda, and Jamaica.<ref name="POWO_90845-1" />

==Cultivation and uses==
''Heptapleurum arboricola'' is commonly grown as a [[houseplant]], popular for its tolerance of neglect and poor growing conditions. It is also grown as a landscape (garden) plant in milder climates where frosts are not severe. Numerous [[cultivar]]s have been selected for variations in leaf colour and pattern, often [[variegation|variegated]] with creamy-white to yellow edges or centres, and [[dwarfing|dwarf]] forms. The cultivar 'Gold Capella' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/58935/Schefflera-arboricola-Gold-Capella/Details |title=''Schefflera arboricola'' 'Gold Capella' |publisher=RHS |access-date=5 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf |title=AGM Plants - Ornamental |date=July 2017 |page=95 |publisher=Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=5 November 2018}}</ref>

===Care===
The plant prefers bright indirect light, but can adapt to a wide variety of light levels. As a tropical plant, it prefers moisture and humidity, but soil should be well-drained and allowed to dry out between waterings. Allowing the plant to sit in water can cause root rot. The plant can be propagated through cuttings, which will develop roots when placed in soil or water.<ref name="gardenersworld">{{cite web |title=How to grow and care for umbrella plant |url=https://www.gardenersworld.com/how-to/grow-plants/umbrella-plant-care/ |website=BBC Gardeners World Magazine |publisher=[[BBC Studios]] |access-date=4 January 2024 |date=29 November 2022}}</ref>

===Aerial roots===
Under the right conditions, this plant will produce [[aerial roots]] that, when they reach the ground, will convert to fully functional roots. They give the plant an unusual and interesting appearance. Three conditions must be maintained for the plant to produce them: a high growth rate, insufficient trunk roots (the plant is root bound or these roots are pruned) and constant, very high [[humidity]].{{Citation needed|date=March 2022}}

===Toxicity===
All parts of the plant contain [[calcium oxalate crystals]], [[saponins]] and [[terpenoids]], toxic compounds which are irritants for cats and dogs. They can cause swelling (in some cases leading to breathing difficulties), burning of the mouth, difficulty swallowing, vomiting, diarrhoea, and itching.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dogs, Cats and Umbrella Trees |url=https://animalpoisons.com.au/news/dogs-cats-and-umbrella-trees |website=Animal Poisons Helpline |access-date=4 January 2024 |language=en-AU |date=29 June 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Schefflera {{!}} ASPCA |url=https://www.aspca.org/pet-care/animal-poison-control/toxic-and-non-toxic-plants/schefflera |website=www.aspca.org |publisher=[[American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals]] |access-date=4 January 2024 |language=en}}</ref> For humans, the plant is low-severity poison and a skin irritant which can cause contact dermatitits.<ref>{{cite book |title=HTA Guide to Potentially Harmful Plants |date=2022 |publisher=The [[Horticultural Trades Association]] |page=10 |edition=3 |url=https://hta.org.uk/resources/get?mediaId=8478 |access-date=4 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220723203103/https://hta.org.uk/resources/get?mediaId=8478 |archive-date=23 Jul 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Heptapleurum arboricola (Dwarf Schefflera, Dwarf Umbrella Tree, Hawaiian Umbrella Tree, Octopus Tree, Parasol Plant) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/heptapleurum-arboricola/ |website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu |publisher=[[NC State University]] and [[NC A&T State University]] |access-date=4 January 2024}}</ref>
